## Implementation contract (2026-09-26, post external review)

Written against code facts verified in the 2026-09-26 review; addresses the
external (GPT-5.6) review gaps 1-3 and 5. Gap 4 (cancel verb) is delegated
to [[WK-0144]].

### Core query (dispatch-core)

New `listUnhandledRuns(repoRoot): Promise<Result<UnhandledRun[]>>`, new
module beside `status.ts`.

- `UnhandledRun = { handoff_id, run_id, status, branch, completed_at, note? }`
- Unit: the HO's LATEST terminal run only. Order by `state.json.completed_at`
  — verified stamped on EVERY terminal outcome (single terminal write path,
  `dispatch-controller-entry.ts:337-341`), ties broken by run-id
  lexicographic. A run without `completed_at` is by definition non-terminal
  (or unreadable) and never joins terminal ordering: readable non-terminal
  → suppression rule below; unreadable → its own `unreadable` line. (rev 3:
  earlier mtime fallback deleted — it was an invention; terminal implies
  `completed_at`.)
- Handled evidence (rev 2, after second external review):
  - `delivered|completed`: DISCHARGED iff a review HO exists in
    `wiki/handoffs/` with `base_ref: dispatch/<HO>` AND
    `reviewed_run: <this run's id>` (rev 3: run-specific — all runs of an
    HO share one branch, so a stale review of run N must not discharge
    run N+1; `derive-review` gains a `reviewed_run` stamp, set to the HO's
    latest terminal run id at derivation time, `derive-review.ts` createOpts).
    Merge is subsumed by review evidence: `merge-delivery` refuses to merge
    without it, so every kb merge is preceded by it. OR the run dir is gone
    (cleanup). Branch absence alone is NOT evidence — a manual
    `git branch -D` must not silently discharge; merges done outside kb nag
    until cleanup (D2 accepted cost). Legacy review HOs without
    `reviewed_run` discharge nothing — one-time migration cost, cleared by
    cleanup.
  - `failed|refused|cancelled|timed_out`: DISCHARGED iff the run dir is
    gone (cleanup); otherwise nags.
  - SUPPRESSED (not discharged) while a non-terminal run of the same HO
    exists (the per-HO single-flight guard guarantees at most one): an
    in-flight retry is active handling, already visible as `running`. If
    the retry dies without a terminal write, cleaning up the stale run
    re-exposes this line; when the retry reaches terminal state, "latest
    terminal run" moves to it automatically — that is the D2 transfer.
  - Invariant (restated): a line is discharged only by review-derivation or
    cleanup; it may be temporarily suppressed by an in-flight retry, and
    re-emerges if that retry is cleaned up without reaching terminal state.
- Fail loud, not wide: a corrupt/unreadable `state.json` yields an
  `UnhandledRun` with `status: "unreadable"` and a note — never silently
  skipped, never fails the whole query.
- No caching. Scan is bounded by live run dirs; `cleanup` prunes.
- `cleanup` of a run dir also removes all OLDER run dirs of the same HO
  (superseded by definition — rev 3: prevents an older terminal run from
  resurfacing as "latest" after a newer one is cleaned).

### Response contract

- MCP (`create-server.ts`, the single tool-registration loop): before
  serializing any tool result, attach `unhandled_runs: UnhandledRun[]` as a
  STRUCTURED sibling field when non-empty — never prepended text (a text
  preamble corrupts machine-read output; external review finding). Error
  envelopes attach it too when `dir` was resolvable; skip otherwise.
- CLI (`run.ts` `run()` wrapper): banner lines print to STDERR, exactly
  once, AFTER the command's own execution (post-command state — a run
  handled by this very invocation must not nag). Format:
  `⚑ UNHANDLED: <HO> <status> <completed_at> → <branch>`. Stdout stays
  reserved for each command's own output, so `wait-for-run` JSON can never
  be corrupted. If `listUnhandledRuns` itself fails: one stderr line
  `⚑ unhandled-runs check failed: <error code>`, and the command's own
  exit code is left untouched (fail loud, never mask the primary result).
- Server instructions: delete "Read the command's output for the run result
  (JSON)" (`create-server.ts:81`); replace with one line documenting the
  field: "Any response may carry `unhandled_runs`; surface each entry to
  the operator." (Documentation of a deterministic field — the mechanism
  does not depend on the instruction being followed.)

### Mechanical assignments

- Generated watch command (`dispatch-background.ts:279`): drop `--json`,
  add `--timeout-seconds 7200` (2 h; the silent 1800 s default mis-reads
  any run over 30 min as failure).
- `wait-for-run` exit codes (`run.ts`): `0` delivered|completed; `1` any
  other TERMINAL status (failed|refused|cancelled|timed_out); `2` bad
  arguments; `3` watcher gave up with the run still non-terminal; `4` state
  unreadable / wait error. Documented in `HELP_TEXT`.
- Stdout is a JSON object in EVERY case (D4): terminal → the run-result
  JSON; bad args → `{ok:false,error:"BAD_ARGS"}`; watcher timeout →
  `{ok:false,error:"WATCH_TIMEOUT",status:"<last-seen>"}`; unreadable →
  `{ok:false,error:"STATE_UNREADABLE"}`. No outcome prints bare text.
- Output: always the run-result JSON on stdout (D4). `--json` accepted as a
  no-op alias for one release (compatibility courtesy), then removed;
  repo-internal callers drop it immediately.

### Streaming half (ex-WK-0142 scope) — capture-gated

Committed now: one append-only `worker-events.jsonl` per run bundle;
`status` enrichment (turn count, last activity, files touched) is a
projection derived from that single file (external review simplification).
The event schema is `[UNVERIFIED-SHAPE]` and MUST NOT be written from
memory — captures first:

- [x] Capture raw claude worker stdout inside the jail (stream-json vs
  buffered single object)
  (2026-09-26: single buffered JSON object at exit, type:"result"; SRC-0008)
- [x] Capture raw codex worker stdout inside the jail
  (2026-09-26: streaming JSONL — thread.started, turn.started,
  item.started/completed, turn.completed; SRC-0008)
- [x] Capture `claude -p` headless treatment of backgrounded shells
  (2026-09-26: disproven — backgrounded processes are orphaned, not killed;
  watcher pattern is safe for headless use; SRC-0008)

Event schema + projection fields are appended to this contract after the
captures land; they are the only part an implementer may not guess.

# WK-0187: Errored 0-token worker run derives `delivered` via prose_fallback — WK-0091 false-positive class resurfaces on single-message stopReason=error path

## Objective

A run whose only API call errored (HTTP 404, zero tokens, zero output) must never derive
`delivered`. HO-0064/RUN-089e6deb did exactly that: the response doc reads
`outcome: delivered`, `delivery_method: prose_fallback`, `worker_report_chars: 0`,
`total_tokens: 0`, `recovery_valid: false`. DEC-0010's mechanical-completion principle
("completion is structural") is violated in reverse — a structurally empty run passed as
complete.

## Diagnosis (live capture, 2026-09-30)

Run: `.agent-runs/runs/HO-0064/RUN-089e6deb-1009-4e92-a9bf-ac4eed4b769e/` (redteam mode,
`openrouter-openai` / `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`, wiki_commit 46a13dd).

Worker JSONL sequence (from `worker-output.log`): `session` → `agent_start` →
`turn_start` → user `message_start`/`message_end` → assistant `message_start` with
`"stopReason":"error"`, `"errorMessage":"404: ..."`, zero usage → `message_end` →
`turn_end` → `agent_end` → `agent_settled`. Pi settled cleanly (no crash, presumably
exit 0), exactly one assistant message, that message errored, no retry attempts.

The 404 itself: OpenRouter returned "0 endpoints out of 1 requested are available
matching your guardrail restrictions and data policy" (ZDR exclusion of the OpenAI
endpoint — that config problem is [[WK-0189]]; this WK is about the verdict).

Why the ladder passed it:
- [[WK-0091]] (`fe3a2ba`) fixed the false-positive `completed` for the
  all-attempts-errored stream shape. This capture is a different shape: a single
  assistant message with `stopReason: "error"` and a clean `agent_settled` — the
  WK-0091 detection does not fire (exact predicate to be confirmed against
  `adapters/pi.ts` during the fix; DEC-0009: verify against this capture, not memory).
- `deriveVerdict` (`capture.ts:414-461`) for redteam checks `piResult` crash evidence;
  no crash was flagged, so the advisory path proceeded: no diff expected, `no_changes`,
  verdict `delivered` with `delivery_method: prose_fallback` — despite the prose being
  0 chars. For advisory modes the transcript IS the product ([[WK-0183]] semantics);
  an empty product cannot be `delivered`.

## Scope

- Detection: `parsePiOutput` (or verdict ladder) treats a final assistant message with
  `stopReason: "error"` / zero output as worker failure with a distinct stopReason
  (mirror WK-0091's fix shape).
- Backstop: advisory-mode verdict refuses `delivered` when the worker report is empty
  (`worker_report_chars: 0` / no final message) — structural, mode-wide, so the same
  hole is closed for code_review/research (and explore_code when WK-0183 lands). Kin
  to [[WK-0169]]'s 0-byte skeleton filter on the delivery side.
- Golden fixture: this run's `worker-output.log` checked in unedited (DEC-0009) as the
  errored-single-message fixture, with a parse test asserting `failed` (not
  `delivered`).
- Out: the endpoint-eligibility preflight ([[WK-0189]]); unhandled-runs lifecycle
  ([[WK-0188]]).

## Checklist

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying RUN-089e6deb's `worker-output.log` through capture derives `failed`
      with a distinct stopReason, never `delivered` (ruled 2026-09-30: no new
      top-level outcome class — see Notes)
- [ ] Advisory-mode run with empty worker report cannot derive `delivered` (unit test
      per advisory mode)
- [ ] Golden fixture committed from this run's log, unedited, with parse test
- [ ] Existing verdict tests pass unchanged; `npm run typecheck && npm test` clean

## Notes

- Found 2026-09-30 during the first dispatch on the `openrouter-openai` backend
  (HO-0064, redteam of the WK-0183 spec). Reopened IN-0004 (operator ruling: core-loop
  correctness, not an extension).
- Blocks [[WK-0183]]: its Tier 3 live gate relies on `delivered` being meaningful for
  advisory modes; with this bug an empty explore_code run would false-pass the gate.
- The false `delivered` also polluted the unhandled-runs list (HO-0064 now nags as
  delivered) — lifecycle side is [[WK-0188]] (ruled 2026-09-30: reminder removed
  entirely, so the nag side dissolves).
- Outcome vocabulary ruled 2026-09-30 (operator, planner session): reuse `failed`
  plus a distinct stopReason (WK-0091's fix shape); no new top-level outcome class.
  [[WK-0189]]'s "distinct infrastructure-refusal class" is carried by the stopReason
  value, not new vocabulary.

# WK-0188: Unhandled-runs reminder is a permanent nag: no discharge path for advisory/review/terminal-failure runs; full list floods every MCP response

## Objective

The [[WK-0153]] unhandled-runs reminder has accumulated ~30 permanently-nagging runs
(observed 2026-09-30: every `create-handoff` and `dispatch` MCP response carries the
full list, HO-0013 through HO-0064). The reminder was built to surface completions the
operator hasn't acted on; in practice most listed runs WERE acted on (reviewed, merged,
shipped — e.g. the HO-0060→HO-0063 chain merged at `0a0b04f`) and can never leave the
list. The signal is dead and the payload bloats every orchestrator context.

## Diagnosis (code read, 2026-09-30)

`unhandled-runs.ts` (WK-0153 D2 ruling): "handled" is derived from exactly two disk
facts — (a) a `code_review` HO whose frontmatter carries `base_ref: dispatch/<HO>` +
`reviewed_run: <run id>` discharges that target run, or (b) the run dir is gone
(cleanup). Consequences:

1. **Review runs themselves are undischargeable.** A code_review HO's own run is
   `delivered`, and nothing reviews a review — it nags until its run dir is deleted.
   Same for redteam and research (and explore_code when [[WK-0183]] lands): the
   evidence index only reads `mode: code_review` HOs (`unhandled-runs.ts:87-88`), so
   no advisory run can ever be discharged by evidence.
2. **Non-dischargeable terminal states nag forever.** `DISCHARGEABLE_BY_REVIEW` is
   `{delivered, completed}` only (`unhandled-runs.ts:36`); `failed`/`refused`/
   `cancelled`/`timed_out` runs "nag until their run dir is cleaned up" — and cleanup
   is a manual step nobody runs (HO-0013 `refused` has nagged since 2026-09-20).
3. **Merge is not discharge evidence.** `merge-delivery` gates on review evidence but
   writes no handled-mark the reminder reads; a reviewed-and-merged implement run only
   leaves the list because its reviewing HO carries `reviewed_run` — the review run it
   spawned then joins the list (see 1). Net: every completed dispatch chain leaves at
   least one permanent nag.
4. **Presentation:** the full array is appended to every MCP tool response
   (`create-server.ts` `toErrorEnvelope` + success paths) with no cap, no summary, no
   age filter. At ~30 entries this is pure context tax on every tool call.

## Scope

**Ruled 2026-09-30 (operator, planner session): delete the reminder entirely** —
supersedes the discharge-semantics design question above (and the interim
failures-ack ruling from the same session). Rationale: the mechanism's only
affordance is redelivery-on-next-kb-call; [[WK-0153]]'s own transcript replay shows
the banner would NOT have fired in its motivating incident (no kb call in the
delivery→pushback window); observed miss rate ~1 in 15 dispatches with
minutes-cheap manual recovery; a proper discharge lifecycle costs more than the
affordance is worth. Retires WK-0153's D1/D2 reminder; the watch-command
notification and the `status` pull surface carry the completion signal unchanged.

Removal set (Sonnet blast-radius audit, hand-verified 2026-09-30; rollback tag
`pre-wk0188-reminder-removal` @ 0a0b04f):

- `packages/dispatch-core/src/unhandled-runs.ts` — whole file
- `packages/dispatch-core/src/index.ts:83-85` — exports
- `packages/dispatch-mcp/src/create-server.ts:5,15,18-20,150-157,163-169` — field
  attach + `toErrorEnvelope` param; plus line 99's trailing instruction clause
  ("Any response may carry `unhandled_runs`…")
- `packages/dispatch-cli/src/run.ts:13,494-509` — stderr banner
- `packages/dispatch-core/src/cleanup.ts:151-187` — WK-0153 sibling sweep.
  Purpose-dead once the reminder is gone: its sole consumer was the reminder's
  "latest terminal run" unit (`derive-review.ts:63-90` does its own scan; nothing
  else computes latest-per-HO), and it destroys older run-dir evidence with no
  beneficiary. Cleanup's orphan passes and the `cleanup` tool stay.
- `tests/dispatch-unhandled-runs.test.ts`, `tests/dispatch-cleanup-siblings.test.ts`
  — whole files

MUST NOT change (proof surface): `dispatch-background.ts`, `wait.ts`,
`dispatch-cli/src/run.ts:369-421` (wait-for-run + exit codes),
`create-server.ts` watch/background instruction recipe, `merge-delivery.ts`
(review gate reads response-doc frontmatter, never `reviewed_run` — verified),
`derive-review.ts` (`reviewed_run` stamping stays; the field becomes write-only —
harmless, flagged for future cleanup).

## Checklist

## Acceptance criteria

(Rewritten 2026-09-30 per the deletion ruling; the original discharge-lifecycle
criteria are superseded.)

- [ ] Removal set deleted; `unhandled_runs` appears nowhere in code or MCP

# WK-0189: Deterministic pre-dispatch endpoint-eligibility preflight: refuse provider-pin/ZDR configs with zero eligible endpoints before spawning a worker

## Objective

A backend config whose provider pin + ZDR/data-policy constraints match zero endpoints
for the requested model should refuse at the gate — before clone, jail, and worker
spawn — not surface as an in-worker HTTP 404 that the verdict ladder then has to
classify. HO-0064 burned a full dispatch cycle (admission passed, jail built, Pi
spawned) to discover a config-level impossibility that was knowable up front.

## Evidence (live capture, 2026-09-30)

RUN-089e6deb (`openrouter-openai` / `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`, `zdr: true`,
`provider.only: ["OpenAI"]`): OpenRouter answered
`404: "0 endpoints out of 1 requested are available matching your guardrail
restrictions and data policy"` with a structured `routing_funnel` in `metadata`:
Initial Endpoints 7 → Regional Surcharge 4 → Tier Endpoint Rows 2 → provider.only 1 →
**Filter by Guardrails 0** (`zdr-violation-by-account` + `zdr-violation-by-guardrail`,
each naming its configure URL). Full JSON in the run's `worker-output.log`. The
constraint set that produced this is static config (`backends.json` request_params +
account settings) plus the model id — nothing about it requires a worker.

## Scope

**Ruled 2026-09-30 (operator, planner session): no per-dispatch preflight.** The
constraint set is static config (`backends.json` request_params + account settings +
model id), so the probe runs at config time, operator-initiated, via
`check-environment` — the dispatch path gains zero code, zero latency, zero
recurring cost. The `NO_ELIGIBLE_ENDPOINT` refusal code and any admission change
are dropped; this record's "refuse at gate" title framing is superseded.

- Probe (rule 17: deterministic, plain code): for each configured pi-family
  backend×model carrying `request_params.provider`/`zdr` constraints, one minimal
  dry-run completion (minimal max_tokens); 404-vs-200 IS the verdict. Report
  eligible/ineligible per pair, echoing OpenRouter's `ineligibility_reasons`
  verbatim plus the configure URLs. Home: `packages/dispatch-core/src/environment.ts`,
  joining the WK-0174 per-backend probe pattern (`probeCliReachability`,
  `environment.ts:306-309`).
- Evidence: the 404 body shape is already captured (RUN-089e6deb
  `worker-output.log`); an eligible 200 is a normal completion — no
  `[UNVERIFIED-SHAPE]` remains, no capture task gates the build. The
  endpoints-listing candidate is DROPPED: it would need its own capture plus an
  unverified assumption that the listing evaluates account-level ZDR guardrails
  (the captured exclusions were `zdr-violation-by-account`).
- Backstop for a skipped check: [[WK-0187]]'s detection (ruled same day: `failed` +
  distinct stopReason) makes the in-worker 404 loud and correctly classified — one
  dispatch cycle lost, never a false `delivered`. No separate infra-refusal outcome
  class.
- Out: any change to the operator's ZDR posture itself (that ruling is pending,
  session 2026-09-30); auto-editing account settings (operator-only, per SRC-0009
  trust model).

## Checklist

## Acceptance criteria

(Rewritten 2026-09-30 per the check-environment ruling.)

- [ ] `check-environment` against the current config reports `openrouter-openai` /

  flag cleared, but account-level ZDR settings + the default-workspace guardrail

  config-side relaxing alone is insufficient — exactly the account-state class
  the check-environment probe will surface.**
- Ruled 2026-09-30: probe moved to `check-environment` (config-time, one-shot) —

# WK-0153: Background dispatch notification is instruction-dependent: watcher result trapped in temp file, orchestrator must Read it

## Objective

Find a notification mechanism for dispatch run completion that does not
depend on an LLM following an instruction. The current mechanism (WK-0132
"RESOLVED" section) failed live on 2026-09-26: the watcher exited, the
orchestrator got "exit 0", never read the temp file, and reported the run
as hung when it had already delivered.

## Evidence

### The failure (2026-09-26, HO-0014 dispatch from kb)

> Steps 6-8 below are contradicted by the session transcript — see
> §Review findings → Evidence corrections.

1. `dispatch` MCP tool returned `{ runId, watch: "npx tsx ... wait-for-run --json" }`
2. Orchestrator ran the watch command as `Bash(cmd, run_in_background: true)`
3. Worker ran 20 minutes, delivered, controller wrote `state.json: delivered`
4. `wait-for-run` saw terminal status, printed JSON to stdout, exited 0
5. Claude Code task-notification arrived: `"Background command ... completed (exit code 0)"`
6. Notification carried: exit code, output_file path. Did NOT carry: run status, HO id, branch name
7. Orchestrator did not read the output file — reported the run as hung
8. Operator manually asked "what is happening?" — orchestrator checked process I/O, confirmed active work, but never surfaced the completion

### The constraint triangle

| Constraint | Source | Implication |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Fire-and-forget | DEC-0014: dispatch always background, no blocking MCP calls | Result must arrive asynchronously |
| No instruction-dependence | Operator ruling 2026-09-26 | Cannot rely on "the model should Read the file" |
| No session blocking | WK-0132: wait-for-run retired as MCP tool because it blocks | Cannot use a synchronous MCP tool to wait |

### Two notification mechanisms in Claude Code

| Mechanism | Result delivery | Deterministic? |
|-----------|----------------|----------------|
| Agent tool (SubagentHandback) | Inline to parent conversation | Yes — result arrives without any action by the parent |
| Bash run_in_background | stdout → temp file; notification says "exit 0" | No — parent must proactively Read the output file |

Dispatch uses mechanism #2. So do agent_resume_builder and bioinfo-agent-toolkit
catalog intake (WK-0132 Capture 5). All three have the same gap.

### MCP protocol options (from WK-0132 Capture 4, 2026-09-20)

- `notifications/progress`: in-flight only, not post-return
- `notifications/resources/updated`: subscribe/push, client support unverified
- `notifications/tasks/status`: experimental, Claude Code does NOT implement (GitHub #18617 closed "not planned", #31427 closed duplicate)

### Why --json on the watch command

`dispatch-background.ts:279` hardcodes `--json` because the MCP server
instructions say "Read the command's output for the run result (JSON)."
The flag exists to serve the instruction-dependent pattern.

## Scope

Investigation. Find a mechanism that satisfies the constraint triangle.
Candidate directions (unvetted — investigation must validate or reject each):

1. **wait-for-run writes result to a well-known location in the run bundle**
   + something deterministically surfaces it (what surfaces it without an
   instruction? unclear — this is the gap)
2. **Agent tool wrapper** around the poll loop — SubagentHandback delivers
   inline, but wastes an LLM agent on a 20-minute poll loop
3. **Claude Code platform change** — task-notification includes command
   stdout (or last N bytes) — would fix dispatch, resume_builder, and
   catalog intake simultaneously, but is external to kb
4. **Something else** — the investigation's job to find it

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] At least one mechanism identified that satisfies all three constraints
  (unhandled-runs reminder, ruled D1=A/D2=A 2026-09-26)
- [x] If the mechanism requires a kb code change, the change is specced (file, function, what changes)
  (§Implementation contract, 2026-09-26; streaming event schema deliberately
  capture-gated, not guessed)
- [x] If the mechanism requires a Claude Code platform feature, that dependency is stated explicitly
  (none required — mechanism is deliberately tool-agnostic per operator ruling)
- [x] If no mechanism exists within current constraints, that conclusion is stated with evidence
  (n/a — mechanism found)

## Review findings (2026-09-26, orchestrator review)

### Operator ruling (2026-09-26)

No kb tool may be Claude-specific. Any mechanism must work for any
orchestrator (Claude Code, codex, headless script). Claude Code hooks, MCP
channels, and Agent-tool wrappers are out as the primary mechanism.

### Evidence corrections (from transcript)

Source: `~/.claude/projects/-home-mcap91-projects-kb/89ca2ecc-6d10-4cd2-bb8b-8d74855e471b.jsonl`
(orchestrator model `claude-opus-4-6`).

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|-----------|-------|
| 19:06:36 | `dispatch` HO-0014 |
| 19:06:41 | watch backgrounded; model-authored description "Watch HO-0014 dispatch run until terminal status" |
| 19:15:34 | **Operator**: "seems like it is hung, same as last time" — run still in progress (minute 9 of ~20) |
| 19:17:29 | Orchestrator reads `/proc/<pid>/io`, correctly reports "actively working" |
| ~19:26 | Orchestrator mid-turn running a `kill` (target not verified) |
| 19:26:21 | Run delivered; `state.json` terminal |
| 19:26:22 | Notification arrives in the same turn as the kill result: `Background command "Watch HO-0014 dispatch run until terminal status" completed (exit code 0)` |

Corrections to §Evidence:
- Step 6: the notification carried the HO id (via the Bash description) and
  exit 0, which `run.ts:347-358` maps to `delivered|completed`. The signal
  was sufficient.
- Step 7: "hung" came from the operator 11 min before delivery, not from the
  orchestrator after delivery.
- Step 8: the `/proc` check ran 19:15-19:17 while the run was genuinely
  active; its conclusion was correct.

### Root causes (revised)

- **RC1 — nothing brings a skipped completion back.** The notification arrived
  mid-turn and was dropped; no later surface re-shows it. Content was not the
  problem — inlining stdout (candidate 3) would not have changed the outcome.
- **RC2 — no mid-run visibility ([[WK-0142]]).** `worker-output.log` at 0 bytes
  made a healthy run look hung, which started the investigation and kill that
  buried the notification. Same incident, not a sibling.
- **RC3 (unverified) — raw `kill` in flight at delivery.** If it targeted the
  run, it raced the controller. No state-checked cancel verb exists.

### Candidate verdicts

1. Well-known location + surfacer — **keep**. Location exists:
   `.agent-runs/runs/<HO>/<run>/state.json` (gitignored). Surfacer must be
   kb-side (ruling above).
2. Agent-tool wrapper — **reject**. Claude-specific; subagent results also
   arrive as mid-turn notifications (same RC1 exposure).
3. Platform stdout-in-notification — **reject as the fix**. External; does
   not address RC1.
4. MCP channels (new) — **reject**. Claude-specific research preview (plugin +
   `--channels` flag + org gate).
5. Claude Code hooks (Stop block / UserPromptSubmit context) (new) — **reject
   as primary** per ruling. Possible optional per-app adapter later.

### Blast radius missed by original scope

- Watch timeout: `dispatch-background.ts:279` passes no `--timeout-seconds`
  (default 1800s, `wait.ts:10`). A run >30 min exits 1 with status `running`
  → reads as failure.
- Exit 1 conflates failed / refused / timed_out / cancelled / still-running /
  bad args (`run.ts:347-371`).
- Headless: in `claude -p`, plain background shells are killed ~5s after the
  final result (Claude Code docs, headless.md — `[UNVERIFIED-SHAPE]`, docs
  only). The watch pattern cannot serve [[WK-0106]] as-is.
- No post-terminal "handled" state exists anywhere (`consumed`/`rejected` are
  launch-token states only — `types.ts:252-253`, `status.ts:367-368`,
  `lookup.ts:41-42`; citation corrected 2026-09-26, was `paths.ts:9`).
- Session loss: the watcher dies with the session; nothing re-surfaces a
  completion after restart or compaction.
- Concurrency: `ACTIVE_RUN_EXISTS` is per-HO (`dispatch-background.ts:139-164`),
  so cross-HO runs overlap.
- resume_builder and catalog intake cannot be fixed by a kb-dispatch change —
  out of scope for this WK.

### Proposed direction (tool-agnostic, pending D1)

- **Wake-up:** keep the watch command — "a command exited" works in every
  orchestrator.
- **Delivery:** every kb-dispatch response (MCP and CLI) leads with
  finished-but-unhandled runs, one line each, until handled.
- **Reuse:** `state.json`, `status`, response docs, and the
  `derive-review` → `merge-delivery` chain.
- **Simplify:** watch always prints the run-result JSON (D4 ruling: no
  plain-line mode, `--json` flag retired); delete the recipe instruction
  "Read the command's output for the run result (JSON)" (`create-server.ts:82`).

### Open decisions (operator)

**D1 — What does kb promise on completion?**
- A (recommended): "can be missed once, can't be lost" — every kb response
  repeats unhandled completions until handled. Works in any orchestrator.
  Limit: if nothing calls kb, nobody hears.
- B: "can't be missed" — requires per-app interrupt mechanisms (Claude Code
  hooks etc.); conflicts with the ruling unless built as optional adapters
  over A.

**Ruled 2026-09-26 (operator): A.** Reasoning: B needs per-app interrupt
machinery (Claude-specific hooks), barred by the portability ruling above —
and even an interrupt lands as skimmable text, so B cannot actually deliver
"can't be missed" (delivery ≠ attention, proven by this incident: the
notification arrived 0.5s before the kill and was still skipped).
Constraints attached to the ruling:
- The reminder line states FACTS only (HO id, terminal status, branch,
  timestamp) — never instructions. This keeps [[DEC-0028]] ruling 4
  ("status is diagnostic") intact; see the DEC-0028 amendment note.
- Coverage framing: this reminder and [[WK-0142]] cover different failure
  windows (post-completion forgetting vs mid-run blindness) — complementary,
  not redundant; neither substitutes for the other.
- DEC-0028's deferral premise ("task-notifications will be the permanent
  completion surface") collapsed with this incident; DEC-0028 is amended,
  not reversed.

**D2 — What clears the reminder ("handled")?**
- A: derived from existing state — the run's next step happened (review
  derived, merged, re-dispatched, or cleaned up). No new bookkeeping; repeats
  for deliberately abandoned runs until cleanup.
- B: explicit acknowledge marker + command. Precise; adds a file and a verb.

**Ruled 2026-09-26 (operator): A.** "Handled" is derived from existing disk
state only — review derived, merged, re-dispatched, or cleaned up (all four
verified checkable today: response doc, review HO with matching `base_ref`,
branch deletion + merge commit, run-dir removal). No new marker file, no new
verb. Accepted cost: a deliberately abandoned run nags until `cleanup` —
which is the correct pressure, since B would allow dismissing a run without
acting on it, re-opening the forgetting gap.

Clarification (operator probe, 2026-09-26): "re-dispatched" TRANSFERS the
obligation, never discharges it. The reminder unit is the HO's latest
terminal run — a re-dispatch of the same HO clears run N's line only
because run N+1 raises its own line at its terminal state (and delivers to
the same per-HO branch `dispatch/<HO>`, superseding run N's delivery). A
dispatch of a different HO clears nothing. Invariant for the build: a
banner may change which run it names; it may not disappear without a
derived review, a merge, or an explicit cleanup.

Concurrency (operator probe, 2026-09-26): the reminder is a LIST, one line
per unhandled terminal run, each cleared independently. All clear evidence
is keyed to the run's own HO id (review `base_ref: dispatch/<HO>`, deletion
of branch `dispatch/<HO>`, run dir under `runs/<HO>/`) — no activity on one
HO can clear another HO's line, no matter how many runs are in flight.

**D3 — Scope.** Fold RC2 (WK-0142 mid-run progress) and RC3 (state-checked
cancel verb) into this WK, or keep separate and link?

**Ruled 2026-09-26 (operator): combine.** [[WK-0142]] folds into this WK's
build. Rationale: transcript replay (session `89ca2ecc`, verified 2026-09-26)
showed the missed notification was downstream of zero mid-run visibility —
RC2 caused the hung-look, the investigation, and the busy turn that buried
the notification. The reminder banner alone would NOT have fired during the
incident window (no kb-dispatch tool calls between delivery 19:26 and
operator pushback 19:30). Build priority: (1) WK-0142 mid-run progress,
(2) mechanical fixes below, (3) unhandled-runs reminder.
RC3 (state-checked cancel verb) is NOT designed here — it is already specced
as [[WK-0144]] (`stop-run` MCP tool, parked 2026-09-25, found during review
2026-09-26): its "already-terminated run returns ok with a note" AC is
exactly the state-checked property this incident's kill lacked. Delegated
there; WK-0144's scheduling is its own decision.

**D4 — Watch output.** Plain one line by default with `--json` opt-in, or keep
JSON default? Machine callers should rely on exit codes either way.

**Ruled 2026-09-26 (operator): neither — the decision dissolves.** Output is
always the run-result JSON, exit code always set; no `--json` flag, no
plain-line mode. Rationale: a friendly default only had value when the
printed output was the orchestrator's primary signal; under D1/D2 nothing
in the normal path reads the watcher's stdout (the banner carries the news,
machines use exit codes and files). One format, one code path — the flag
existed solely to serve the deleted instruction-dependent pattern and is
retired with it.

### Mechanical fixes (no decision needed)

- Pass an explicit `--timeout-seconds` on the watch command.
- Distinct exit code for "watcher timed out, run still going" vs. run failure.

## Implementation contract (2026-09-26, post external review)

Written against code facts verified in the 2026-09-26 review; addresses the
external (GPT-5.6) review gaps 1-3 and 5. Gap 4 (cancel verb) is delegated
to [[WK-0144]].

### Core query (dispatch-core)

New `listUnhandledRuns(repoRoot): Promise<Result<UnhandledRun[]>>`, new
module beside `status.ts`.

- `UnhandledRun = { handoff_id, run_id, status, branch, completed_at, note? }`
- Unit: the HO's LATEST terminal run only. Order by `state.json.completed_at`
  — verified stamped on EVERY terminal outcome (single terminal write path,
  `dispatch-controller-entry.ts:337-341`), ties broken by run-id
  lexicographic. A run without `completed_at` is by definition non-terminal
  (or unreadable) and never joins terminal ordering: readable non-terminal
  → suppression rule below; unreadable → its own `unreadable` line. (rev 3:
  earlier mtime fallback deleted — it was an invention; terminal implies
  `completed_at`.)
- Handled evidence (rev 2, after second external review):
  - `delivered|completed`: DISCHARGED iff a review HO exists in
    `wiki/handoffs/` with `base_ref: dispatch/<HO>` AND
    `reviewed_run: <this run's id>` (rev 3: run-specific — all runs of an
    HO share one branch, so a stale review of run N must not discharge
    run N+1; `derive-review` gains a `reviewed_run` stamp, set to the HO's
    latest terminal run id at derivation time, `derive-review.ts` createOpts).
    Merge is subsumed by review evidence: `merge-delivery` refuses to merge
    without it, so every kb merge is preceded by it. OR the run dir is gone
    (cleanup). Branch absence alone is NOT evidence — a manual
    `git branch -D` must not silently discharge; merges done outside kb nag
    until cleanup (D2 accepted cost). Legacy review HOs without
    `reviewed_run` discharge nothing — one-time migration cost, cleared by
    cleanup.
  - `failed|refused|cancelled|timed_out`: DISCHARGED iff the run dir is
    gone (cleanup); otherwise nags.
  - SUPPRESSED (not discharged) while a non-terminal run of the same HO
    exists (the per-HO single-flight guard guarantees at most one): an
    in-flight retry is active handling, already visible as `running`. If
    the retry dies without a terminal write, cleaning up the stale run
    re-exposes this line; when the retry reaches terminal state, "latest
    terminal run" moves to it automatically — that is the D2 transfer.
  - Invariant (restated): a line is discharged only by review-derivation or
    cleanup; it may be temporarily suppressed by an in-flight retry, and
    re-emerges if that retry is cleaned up without reaching terminal state.
- Fail loud, not wide: a corrupt/unreadable `state.json` yields an
  `UnhandledRun` with `status: "unreadable"` and a note — never silently
  skipped, never fails the whole query.
- No caching. Scan is bounded by live run dirs; `cleanup` prunes.
- `cleanup` of a run dir also removes all OLDER run dirs of the same HO
  (superseded by definition — rev 3: prevents an older terminal run from
  resurfacing as "latest" after a newer one is cleaned).

### Response contract

- MCP (`create-server.ts`, the single tool-registration loop): before
  serializing any tool result, attach `unhandled_runs: UnhandledRun[]` as a
  STRUCTURED sibling field when non-empty — never prepended text (a text
  preamble corrupts machine-read output; external review finding). Error
  envelopes attach it too when `dir` was resolvable; skip otherwise.
- CLI (`run.ts` `run()` wrapper): banner lines print to STDERR, exactly
  once, AFTER the command's own execution (post-command state — a run
  handled by this very invocation must not nag). Format:
  `⚑ UNHANDLED: <HO> <status> <completed_at> → <branch>`. Stdout stays
  reserved for each command's own output, so `wait-for-run` JSON can never
  be corrupted. If `listUnhandledRuns` itself fails: one stderr line
  `⚑ unhandled-runs check failed: <error code>`, and the command's own
  exit code is left untouched (fail loud, never mask the primary result).
- Server instructions: delete "Read the command's output for the run result
  (JSON)" (`create-server.ts:81`); replace with one line documenting the
  field: "Any response may carry `unhandled_runs`; surface each entry to
  the operator." (Documentation of a deterministic field — the mechanism
  does not depend on the instruction being followed.)

### Mechanical assignments

- Generated watch command (`dispatch-background.ts:279`): drop `--json`,
  add `--timeout-seconds 7200` (2 h; the silent 1800 s default mis-reads
  any run over 30 min as failure).
- `wait-for-run` exit codes (`run.ts`): `0` delivered|completed; `1` any
  other TERMINAL status (failed|refused|cancelled|timed_out); `2` bad
  arguments; `3` watcher gave up with the run still non-terminal; `4` state
  unreadable / wait error. Documented in `HELP_TEXT`.
- Stdout is a JSON object in EVERY case (D4): terminal → the run-result
  JSON; bad args → `{ok:false,error:"BAD_ARGS"}`; watcher timeout →
  `{ok:false,error:"WATCH_TIMEOUT",status:"<last-seen>"}`; unreadable →
  `{ok:false,error:"STATE_UNREADABLE"}`. No outcome prints bare text.
- Output: always the run-result JSON on stdout (D4). `--json` accepted as a
  no-op alias for one release (compatibility courtesy), then removed;
  repo-internal callers drop it immediately.

### Streaming half (ex-WK-0142 scope) — capture-gated

Committed now: one append-only `worker-events.jsonl` per run bundle;
`status` enrichment (turn count, last activity, files touched) is a
projection derived from that single file (external review simplification).
The event schema is `[UNVERIFIED-SHAPE]` and MUST NOT be written from
memory — captures first:

- [x] Capture raw claude worker stdout inside the jail (stream-json vs
  buffered single object)
  (2026-09-26: single buffered JSON object at exit, type:"result"; SRC-0008)
- [x] Capture raw codex worker stdout inside the jail
  (2026-09-26: streaming JSONL — thread.started, turn.started,
  item.started/completed, turn.completed; SRC-0008)
- [x] Capture `claude -p` headless treatment of backgrounded shells
  (2026-09-26: disproven — backgrounded processes are orphaned, not killed;
  watcher pattern is safe for headless use; SRC-0008)

Event schema + projection fields are appended to this contract after the
captures land; they are the only part an implementer may not guess.
